prompt:
Normalize the single contact record in the user message. Respond only with one JSON object containing exactly the keys "name", "phone", "email", "company", and "country". Each value must be a JSON string or null. No surrounding prose or Markdown.

Extract: Use only the contact-record block, whose label/value lines can occur in any order and use colon, equals, or tab separators. Labels vary. Read the value after the label separator without splitting its contents again. Ignore all surrounding notes and signatures. Trim values and collapse whitespace runs to a single space. Treat absent lines, empty values, and these case-insensitive placeholders as missing: -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD.

Route: A record value containing @ is the email. A value is the phone when, after dropping a leading tel: and a trailing extension of the form ext. N, ext N, xN, #N, or extension N (N is digits), it has at least seven digits and contains only digits, spaces, and + - ( ) . /. Use these content tests regardless of the phone/email labels. For name and company, swap their labeled values if the name-labeled value has a trailing legal suffix and the company-labeled value does not. Recognize these complete suffixes case-insensitively, including when preceded by a comma: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Take explicit country only from the country line.

Normalize the country line to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Accept English, Swedish, and German country names, alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes, and common aliases, all case-insensitively. UK and Great Britain map to GB; Holland to NL; USA and U.S.A. to US; Türkiye to TR; Czech Republic to CZ.

Resolve the phone and country:
- After removing tel: and the extension, ignore an opening parenthesis for prefix detection. A leading + or 00 means international. Delete (0) before stripping spaces, dashes, dots, slashes, and parentheses; replace the compact number's initial 00 with +. Keep the written calling code, even when it disagrees with the country line. Only when the country line is missing (absent, empty, or a placeholder), fill country from this calling code if it belongs to exactly one country. Shared codes, including +1 and +7, do not fill country.
- Otherwise the phone is national. With no country, return null for phone. With a country, strip formatting, remove one leading trunk zero, and prepend + and that country's calling code.
- A non-null phone is E.164: + followed by the calling code and national significant number, digits only after the +.

Normalize the remaining text: For name, split at the first comma if present and put the part after it first. Remove leading honorifics Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, and Prof, case-insensitively, with or without a period. For every space- or hyphen-separated name part, uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest. For company, strip the trailing legal suffix as a whole, along with an optional preceding comma, then uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word. For email, strip surrounding angle brackets and a mailto: prefix, whichever is outermost first if both occur, then lowercase the whole address. Keep Unicode letters and diacritics; do not transliterate. Trim the results and keep whitespace collapsed; Unicode comparison is under NFC.

Use null for missing fields, with the unique international calling-code fallback as the sole exception. Never fill a field from notes, signatures, email domains, company suffixes, or any other inference.
